# Scope and verification claims

This notebook verifies Phase 1 of `magnetofluidics_pinn`
(`v0.1.6+`, single spherical particle, uniform magnetic field, steady
Stokes flow, straight channel) against the one case with a closed-form
solution: axisymmetric Hagen–Poiseuille flow
[@happel1983low; @leal2007advanced]. Three components are exercised
together ---the governing-equation residual ([
`physics.fluid_residuals.stokes_residual`](../magnetofluidics_pinn/physics/fluid_residuals.py)),
the trained network's hard-constrained architecture ([
`networks.constraints.apply_hard_wall_constraint`](../magnetofluidics_pinn/networks/constraints.py)
[@lu2021physics]), and the particle-trajectory integrator ([
`trajectory.integrate_trajectory`](../magnetofluidics_pinn/trajectory/integrator.py)).

## What this notebook does not verify

Phase 2 (particle swarms, non-uniform fields) and Phase 3 (Navier–Stokes, bifurcated geometry) are
out of scope ---`boundary_conditions.magnetic_field_bc.gradient_field` and
`biot_savart_field`, and `geometry.build_bifurcation_domain`, remain
unimplemented in this release and are not exercised here. The Faxén-law
finite-size correction [@faxen1922widerstand; @kim2005microhydrodynamics]
is checked only against its own closed-form prediction for this specific
flow (@sec-streamline), not against an independent finite-size
hydrodynamics reference. A non-uniform magnetic field is likewise out of
scope: `integrate_trajectory` itself rejects one (see its own uniformity
guard), so every trajectory check here uses a uniform field, under which
the dipole force vanishes identically [@abbott2020magnetic].

The table below previews every claim this notebook makes, before running
anything expensive — each row is populated with its measured value in
@sec-summary, once the corresponding section has run.

#| label: setup
import time

import torch

RANDOM_SEED = 42
DEVICE = mfp.resolve_device(None)
DTYPE = torch.float32

verification_checks: tuple[mfp.VerificationCheck, ...] = ()

# Reference problem and analytical solution

## Governing equations

In dimensionless axisymmetric cylindrical coordinates $(r^*, z^*)$, the
Stokes momentum and continuity equations read
$$
-\pdv{p^*}{r^*} + \laplacian u_r^* - \frac{u_r^*}{r^{*2}} = 0, \qquad
-\pdv{p^*}{z^*} + \laplacian u_z^* = 0, \qquad
\frac{1}{r^*}\pdv{ (r^* u_r^*)}{r^*} + \pdv{u_z^*}{z^*} = 0.
$$

Driven by the parabolic inlet profile
[`inlet_velocity_condition`](../magnetofluidics_pinn/boundary_conditions/flow_bc.py)
imposes and a fixed outlet gauge pressure, this system has the classical
closed-form solution
$$
u_r^*(r^*, z^*) = 0, \qquad
u_z^*(r^*, z^*) = u_\text{peak}^*\left (1 - \left (\frac{r^*}{R^*}\right)^2\right), \qquad
\pdv{p^*}{z^*} = -\frac{4 u_\text{peak}^*}{R^{*2}},
$$
with the last relation following directly from substituting $u_z^*$ into
the $z$-momentum equation above. Integrating the parabolic profile over a
cross-section gives the reference volumetric flow rate
$$
Q_\text{ref}^* = \int_0^{R^*} u_z^*(r^*)\, 2\pi r^*\, dr^* = \frac{\pi R^{*2} u_\text{peak}^*}{2}.
$$

These three closed forms 
---[`hagen_poiseuille_velocity_field`](../magnetofluidics_pinn/verification/analytical.py),
[`analytical_pressure_gradient`](../magnetofluidics_pinn/verification/analytical.py), and
[`poiseuille_reference_flow_rate`](../magnetofluidics_pinn/physics/conservation.py) —
are every quantitative reference this notebook compares against.

## Configuration and scales

```{python}
#| label: reference-problem
radius = 7.5e-4             # 750µm
reference_velocity =1.0e-3  # 1 mm/s
length = 4.0 * radius       # 3 mm
dynamic_viscosity = 1e-3    # 1 mPa·s
density = 1.0e3             # 1000 kg/m^3

n_epochs = 400
lbfgs_rounds = 4
lbfgs_iterations_per_round = 400

domain_config = mfp.DomainConfig(kind="channel", length=length, radius=radius)
fluid_config = mfp.FluidConfig(
    regime="stokes", dynamic_viscosity=dynamic_viscosity, density=density,
    reference_velocity=reference_velocity, reference_length=domain_config.radius,
)
field_config = mfp.MagneticFieldConfig(source="uniform", magnitude=1.0e-2, orientation=(1.0, 0.0))
particle_config = mfp.ParticleConfig(radius=10.0e-6, magnetic_moment=(1.0e-11, 0.0))

physical_domain = mfp.build_channel_domain(domain_config)
scales = mfp.compute_scales(fluid_config, field_config)
domain = mfp.nondimensionalize_domain(physical_domain, scales)

# The dimensionless inlet centerline velocity: `FluidConfig.reference_velocity`
# is, by construction of `compute_scales`, the physical velocity that maps to
# exactly 1.0, matching `training.trainer`'s own gauge choice.
PEAK_VELOCITY = 1.0
REFERENCE_PRESSURE = 0.0

pd.Series({"domain.radius": domain.radius, "domain.length": domain.length,
           "scales.length [m]": scales.length, "scales.velocity [m/s]": scales.velocity,
           "scales.pressure [Pa]": scales.pressure})
```

```{python}
#| label: reference-quantities
reference_flow_rate = mfp.poiseuille_reference_flow_rate(domain.radius, PEAK_VELOCITY)
reference_pressure_gradient = mfp.analytical_pressure_gradient(domain.radius, PEAK_VELOCITY)

pd.Series({"Q_ref* (analytical)": reference_flow_rate, "dp*/dz* (analytical)": reference_pressure_gradient})
```

## Calibratable verification thresholds

Every tolerance the checks below compare against is collected into one
[`VerificationThresholds`](../magnetofluidics_pinn/verification/reporting.py)
instance, built by
[`default_thresholds`](../magnetofluidics_pinn/verification/reporting.py)
from the reference scales just computed. Two different kinds of bound are
at play: the closed-form checks in @sec-exact-residual and
@sec-structural are floating-point-accuracy questions (bounded by a
multiple of machine epsilon), while the trained-network checks in
@sec-independent-verification are physical-accuracy questions (bounded by
a fraction of a reference quantity ---`peak_velocity`, `reference_flow_rate`,
or the analytical pressure gradient). Every `*_factor` / `*_fraction`
keyword below is a calibratable constant, not a derived physical value---
tighten or loosen any of them without touching
`magnetofluidics_pinn.verification`.

```{python}
#| label: thresholds
thresholds = mfp.default_thresholds(dtype=DTYPE, peak_velocity=PEAK_VELOCITY)
pd.Series(thresholds.__dict__)
```

# Exact differential-operator verification {#sec-exact-residual}

Evaluating `stokes_residual` on the *closed-form* solution isolates the
residual formula itself from any network training question: on an
independent grid, disjoint from every seed used later for training or
held-out evaluation, the residual should sit at machine precision.

A genuine convenience falls out of this flow having $u_r^* \equiv 0$
identically (not merely small): the axisymmetric residual's singular
$1/r^{*2}$ term is multiplied by an operand that is exactly zero in
floating point, so — unlike a trained network, where a small numerical
$u_r^*$ gets amplified near the axis — this grid needs no axis clearance.
A tiny floor (`1e-8`) on $r^*$ is kept purely to avoid an exact-zero draw
tripping `residual_form="standard"`'s own `r > 0` guard.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-exact-residual
#| tbl-cap: "Exact Stokes residual of the closed-form solution, on an independent grid."
EXACT_GRID_SEED = RANDOM_SEED + 1000  # independent of every training/held-out seed below
N_EXACT_GRID_POINTS = 20_000

exact_grid_generator = torch.Generator(device=DEVICE).manual_seed(EXACT_GRID_SEED)
exact_r = (domain.radius * torch.rand(
    N_EXACT_GRID_POINTS, 1, generator=exact_grid_generator, device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE
)).clamp_min(1.0e-8)
exact_z = domain.length * torch.rand(
    N_EXACT_GRID_POINTS, 1, generator=exact_grid_generator, device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE
)
exact_coordinates = torch.cat([exact_r, exact_z], dim=1).requires_grad_(True)


def analytical_network(coordinates: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Closed-form Hagen-Poiseuille field, exposed with the trained-network calling convention."""
    return mfp.hagen_poiseuille_velocity_field(coordinates, domain, PEAK_VELOCITY, REFERENCE_PRESSURE)


exact_residual = mfp.stokes_residual(analytical_network, exact_coordinates, fluid_config, residual_form="standard")
exact_residual_summary = mfp.summarize_residual(exact_residual, ("momentum_r", "momentum_z", "continuity"))
exact_residual_summary
```

```{python}
#| label: check-exact-residual
verification_checks = verification_checks + (
    mfp.evaluate_check(
        "Exact interior residual",
        "Stokes residual of the closed-form solution on an independent grid",
        exact_residual_summary.loc["total", "max_abs"], thresholds.exact_residual_tolerance, "<=",
    ),
)
verification_checks[-1]
```

# Structural boundary/regularity verification {#sec-structural}

`apply_hard_wall_constraint` claims to enforce axis and wall regularity *structurally* — for every parameter value, not
just after training
[@lu2021physics]. The only way to actually test that claim is to probe a **freshly initialized, untrained** network: if
the conditions hold before
a single gradient step, they hold by construction, not by coincidence of
training.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-structural
#| tbl-cap: "Structural axis/wall regularity, probed on an untrained network."
untrained_network = mfp.apply_hard_wall_constraint(
    mfp.build_mlp(n_inputs=2, n_outputs=3, hidden_layers=(32, 32, 32), activation="tanh", device=str(DEVICE)),
    domain,
)
structural_metrics = mfp.evaluate_structural_constraints(
    untrained_network, domain, n_probe_points=2_000, random_seed=EXACT_GRID_SEED + 1,
)
pd.Series(structural_metrics)
```

```{python}
#| label: check-structural
verification_checks = verification_checks + (
    mfp.evaluate_check(
        "Structural regularity",
        "Axis/wall hard-constraint probe on an untrained network",
        max(structural_metrics.values()), thresholds.structural_tolerance, "<=",
    ),
)
verification_checks[-1]
```

# PINN training

::: {.callout-warning title="Reduced, notebook-scale recipe"}
`NOTEBOOK_TRAINING_CONFIG` below reduces the point counts and iteration
budgets from `TrainingConfig()`'s defaults (`n_epochs`: 20 000 → `{python} n_epochs`;
`lbfgs_rounds`: 4 → `{python} lbfgs_rounds`; 
`lbfgs_iterations_per_round`: 500 → `{python} lbfgs_iterations_per_round`, and
proportionate cuts to every collocation-point count) so this notebook
renders in a reasonable time. Every loss weight, `gradient_clip_norm`, and
`residual_form` is left at its package default — this recipe is smaller,
not different. Reproducing the accuracy figures reported in the package's
own convergence testing (@sec-summary's thresholds are calibrated loosely
enough to accommodate this reduced budget) requires the full default
configuration.
:::

```{python}
#| label: training-config
NOTEBOOK_TRAINING_CONFIG = mfp.TrainingConfig(
    n_interior_points=4_000, n_boundary_points=900,
    n_epochs=n_epochs, random_seed=RANDOM_SEED, device=str(DEVICE),
    use_lbfgs_refinement=True,
    lbfgs_n_interior_points=2_000, lbfgs_n_boundary_points=300,
    lbfgs_rounds=lbfgs_rounds, lbfgs_iterations_per_round=lbfgs_iterations_per_round,
)
NOTEBOOK_TRAINING_CONFIG
```

```{python}
#| label: train
raw_network = mfp.build_mlp(n_inputs=2, n_outputs=3, hidden_layers=(32, 32, 32), activation="tanh", device=str(DEVICE))
network = mfp.apply_hard_wall_constraint(raw_network, domain)

training_start = time.perf_counter()
trained_network, training_history = mfp.train(
    network=network, domain=domain, fluid_config=fluid_config, field_config=field_config,
    training_config=NOTEBOOK_TRAINING_CONFIG, verbose=True, log_every=500,
)
print(f"\nTotal training time: {time.perf_counter() - training_start:.1f} s")
training_history.print_summary()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-training-history
#| fig-cap: "Adam + L-BFGS loss convergence, by component."
mfp.plot_training_history(training_history)
```

Loss convergence is a training diagnostic, not a verification result: a
low training loss does not by itself establish physical accuracy against
an independent reference. @sec-independent-verification is where that
claim actually gets tested.

# Independent hydrodynamic verification {#sec-independent-verification}

Every metric below is computed by
[`verification.metrics`](../magnetofluidics_pinn/verification/metrics.py)
against data the training loop never directly optimizes against as a
single scalar: profiles, global/pointwise error fields, the flow-rate
curve, and a held-out residual batch drawn with its own independent seed.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-profile-invariance
#| tbl-cap: "Predicted axial-velocity profile error and invariance across three axial stations."
Z_STATIONS = (0.1 * domain.length, 0.5 * domain.length, 0.9 * domain.length)
RADIAL_GRID = torch.linspace(0.0, domain.radius, 200, device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE)
AXIAL_GRID = torch.linspace(0.0, domain.length, 200, device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE)

profile_evaluation = mfp.evaluate_velocity_profiles(trained_network, domain, Z_STATIONS, RADIAL_GRID, PEAK_VELOCITY)
profile_invariance = mfp.compute_profile_invariance(profile_evaluation)
pd.options.display.float_format = '{:.3e}'.format
profile_invariance
```

```{python}
#| label: global-pointwise-error
global_l2_error = mfp.compute_global_l2_error(trained_network, domain, RADIAL_GRID, AXIAL_GRID, PEAK_VELOCITY)
max_pointwise_error = mfp.compute_max_pointwise_error(trained_network, domain, RADIAL_GRID, AXIAL_GRID, PEAK_VELOCITY)
pd.Series({"Global relative L2 error": global_l2_error, "Max pointwise velocity error": max_pointwise_error})
```

```{python}
#| label: leakage
leakage_metrics = mfp.compute_radial_leakage(profile_evaluation, PEAK_VELOCITY)
pd.Series(leakage_metrics)
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-flow-rate
#| tbl-cap: "Predicted volumetric flow rate Q(z) versus the analytical reference."
flow_rate_curve = mfp.compute_flow_rate_curve(trained_network, domain, AXIAL_GRID, n_quadrature_points=64)
flow_rate_errors = mfp.compute_flow_rate_errors(flow_rate_curve, reference_flow_rate)
pd.Series(flow_rate_errors)
```

```{python}
#| label: pressure-gradient
pressure_gradient_metrics = mfp.compute_pressure_gradient_error(
    trained_network, domain, PEAK_VELOCITY, n_axial_points=100
)
pd.Series(pressure_gradient_metrics)
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-held-out-residual
#| tbl-cap: "Stokes residual on a held-out collocation batch, independent of every training-time seed."
held_out_residual = mfp.evaluate_held_out_residual(
    trained_network, domain, fluid_config, random_seed=EXACT_GRID_SEED + 2, n_points=5_000,
    residual_form=NOTEBOOK_TRAINING_CONFIG.residual_form,
    axis_clearance_fraction=NOTEBOOK_TRAINING_CONFIG.axis_clearance_fraction,
)
held_out_residual
```

```{python}
#| label: check-independent-verification
verification_checks = verification_checks + (
    mfp.evaluate_check(
        "Global relative L2 error",
        "Relative L2 error of the predicted velocity against the analytical profile",
        global_l2_error, thresholds.global_l2_tolerance, "<=",
    ),
    mfp.evaluate_check(
        "Max pointwise velocity error",
        "Largest pointwise velocity deviation from the analytical profile",
        max_pointwise_error, thresholds.max_pointwise_tolerance, "<=",
    ),
    mfp.evaluate_check(
        "Profile invariance",
        "Consistency of the predicted u_z(r) profile across axial stations",
        profile_invariance["max_abs_deviation_from_mean_profile"].max(), thresholds.max_pointwise_tolerance, "<=",
    ),
    mfp.evaluate_check(
        "Radial leakage",
        "Normalized max |u_r|, relative to the centerline velocity",
        leakage_metrics["normalized_radial_leakage"], thresholds.normalized_leakage_tolerance, "<=",
    ),
    mfp.evaluate_check(
        "Flow-rate conservation",
        "Relative error of Q(z) against the analytical reference flow rate",
        flow_rate_errors["max_relative_flow_rate_error"], thresholds.flow_rate_relative_tolerance, "<=",
    ),
    mfp.evaluate_check(
        "Pressure-gradient fit",
        "Relative error of the fitted dp/dz against the analytical value",
        pressure_gradient_metrics["relative_error"], thresholds.pressure_gradient_relative_tolerance, "<=",
    ),
    mfp.evaluate_check(
        "Held-out PDE residual",
        "Stokes residual RMS on a fresh, independent collocation batch",
        held_out_residual.loc["total", "rms"], thresholds.held_out_residual_tolerance, "<=",
    ),
)
mfp.render_verification_table(verification_checks[-7:])
```

# Single-particle streamline verification {#sec-streamline}

Under a uniform field, a point tracer ($a^*=0$) is advected by the flow
alone (@sec-exact-residual's closed form for $u_z^*$), giving the exact
streamline
[`analytical_tracer_streamline`](../magnetofluidics_pinn/verification/analytical.py)
computes. `nondimensionalize_mobility` is used below for the (unused, at
$a^*=0$) magnetic-drift term only — with a uniform field the dipole force
is exactly zero regardless of the mobility tensor's value.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-streamline
#| tbl-cap: "Point-tracer trajectory versus the closed-form streamline (final rows)."
initial_position_dimensionless = (0.3 * domain.radius, 0.05 * domain.length)
initial_state = mfp.ParticleState(
    position=torch.tensor(initial_position_dimensionless, device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE),
    velocity=torch.zeros(2, device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE),
    time=0.0,
)
field_fn = lambda coordinates: mfp.uniform_field(
    coordinates, magnitude=field_config.magnitude, orientation=field_config.orientation
)
mobility = mfp.nondimensionalize_mobility(particle_config, fluid_config, scales).unsqueeze(0)

trajectories = mfp.integrate_trajectory(
    flow_network=trained_network, field_fn=field_fn, domain=domain, scales=scales,
    particle_config=particle_config, initial_states=[initial_state], mobility_tensor=mobility,
    time_span=(0.0, 5.0), enforce_uniform_field=True, verbose=False,
)
trajectory_comparison = mfp.compare_trajectory_to_analytical(
    trajectories[0], initial_position=initial_position_dimensionless, peak_velocity=PEAK_VELOCITY,
    radius=domain.radius, particle_radius=0.0,
)
trajectory_comparison.tail()
```

```{python}
#| label: check-streamline
verification_checks = verification_checks + (
    mfp.evaluate_check(
        "Streamline alignment",
        "Point-tracer trajectory error against the analytical streamline",
        trajectory_comparison["axial_error"].max(), thresholds.max_pointwise_tolerance * domain.length, "<=",
    ),
)
verification_checks[-1]
```

## Aside: closed-form Faxén offset

$\laplacian u_z^*$ is spatially constant for Hagen–Poiseuille flow (see
@sec-exact-residual's derivation), so Faxén's first law
[@faxen1922widerstand; @kim2005microhydrodynamics] reduces to a single,
position-independent velocity offset rather than a function of $r^*$:

$$
U_z^\text{Faxén} = u_z^*(r_0^*) - \frac{2}{3}\frac{a^{*2}}{R^{*2}} u_\text{peak}^*, \qquad
U_r^\text{Faxén} = 0,
$$

since $u_r^* \equiv 0$ and its Laplacian vanishes identically. This is not
part of the core verification matrix above — no independent finite-size
reference is being checked, only that
[`integrate_trajectory`](../magnetofluidics_pinn/trajectory/integrator.py)'s
own Faxén-corrected drift matches this closed form for the one flow where
it is available analytically.

```{python}
#| label: faxen-aside
a_star = mfp.nondimensionalize_particle(particle_config, scales)
faxen_offset = mfp.faxen_offset_velocity(PEAK_VELOCITY, domain.radius, a_star)

faxen_trajectories = mfp.integrate_trajectory(
    flow_network=trained_network, field_fn=field_fn, domain=domain, scales=scales,
    particle_config=particle_config, initial_states=[initial_state], mobility_tensor=mobility,
    time_span=(0.0, 5.0), enforce_uniform_field=True, verbose=False,
)
faxen_comparison = mfp.compare_trajectory_to_analytical(
    faxen_trajectories[0], initial_position=initial_position_dimensionless, peak_velocity=PEAK_VELOCITY,
    radius=domain.radius, particle_radius=a_star,
)
print(f"a* = {a_star:.4e}   Faxén offset = {faxen_offset:.4e}")
faxen_comparison.tail()
```
